items.author: Hong Kong Free Press
items.title: ‘Who will respond?’: Jailed Hong Kong pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong fears being forgotten amid 10-year sentence
items.summary: The 30-year-old pro-democracy activist has spent almost six years behind bars and was set for release in January 2026, until authorities charged him with conspiring to foreign collusion last year.

items.author: Forus
items.title: Diversifying funding was supposed to protect civil society: It did not
items.summary: A survey of 195 organisations across more than 68 countries shows how the global aid retreat is hitting organizations that spent years building diverse funding streams — and why the crisis goes far beyond money.

items.author: Jude Pierre Louis
items.title: Street medicine vendors are dangerously filling Haiti’s healthcare gaps
items.summary: Street medicine vendors have no professional medical training — and the drugs they sell in questionable conditions on the street pose a serious danger to consumers’ lives.

items.author: Mong Palatino
items.title: In win against impunity, Indonesian court orders the reform of Military Justice Law
items.summary: "Justice for civilian victims of military abuses shouldn’t be blocked by an unfair military court system."

items.author: Masudul Zarif
items.title: Civil society questions decree that could block access to telecommunications networks in Mozambique
items.summary: The telecommunications decree in Mozambique raises serious concerns regarding potential restrictions on fundamental rights, including freedom of expression and access to information during periods of political tension.

items.author: Walid El Houri
items.title: Making injustice legal: How Israeli law legitimizes apartheid, genocide and impunity
items.summary: From military courts to closed investigations, Israeli law enforces two systems to maintain an apartheid, and international accountability is being dismantled by sanctions against the courts that uphold international law.

items.author: Rebecca Cluett
items.title: Madagascar aims to support biodiversity by protecting marine areas
items.summary: At the annual COP17 on biodiversity, Madagascar confirmed its commitment to the 30x30 Global Target and the conservation of its natural heritage.

items.author: Masudul Zarif
items.title: Learning under trees in the era of AI: The paradox of education in Mozambique
items.summary: Mozambique faces an educational paradox: While the use of artificial intelligence is being debated, thousands of students still learn outdoors, without basic infrastructure or internet access.

items.author: Global Voices Eurasia
items.title: Letter from a jailed Azerbaijani political prisoner reveals deadly consequences of silence
items.summary: Bahruz Samadov: “The selective attitude to the human rights issues and turning the blind eye to our suffering endangers the democratic security of the US itself, not to mention its international image.”

items.author: Daria Dergacheva
items.title: While Russia tries to manipulate information, local civil society is teaching Armenians media literacy
items.summary: With the proliferation of generative AI, disinformation and propaganda campaigns have become increasingly sophisticated. Armenia’s experience shows how they operate in a country moving away from its longstanding reliance on Russia.
